records.title: Evaluation of Large Language Models' Capabilities in the Field of Mechanical Engineering
records.reason: This paper systematically evaluates the capabilities of fourteen Large language models(LLMs) in the domain of mechanical engineering. First, we develop a specialized test bank tailored for large models in the mechanical field, comprising various question formats including single-choice, multiple-choice, true/false, and fill-in-the-blank items. Subsequently, we conduct assessments on models including DeepSeek-v3/R1, Claude-opus-4.0, GPT-4.1, Qwen2.5, and KiMi. The evaluation results indicate that DeepSeek-v3pro and Qwen2.5 outperform other models in terms of knowledge accuracy, achieving accuracy rates of 83.72% and 79.19%, respectively.

records.title: TA-MOE: Multi-View Mixture of Experts with Tail-Aware Gating for Long-Tailed Specific Emitter Identification
records.reason: Specific Emitter Identification (SEI) in real-world deployments suffers from severe long-tailed class distributions. Existing single network approaches allow head classes to dominate the shared feature space, while direct application of Mixtureof-Experts (MoE) models introduces further issues of representational homogeneity and gating bias toward majority classes. This paper proposes TA-MoE, a tail-aware Mixture-of-Experts network for long-tailed SEI. TA-MoE employs three heterogeneous experts effectively decoupling feature space competition. A class distribution-aware gating mechanism incorporates class frequency priors. Furthermore, a dual-layer regularization scheme jointly optimizes expert load balance and tail-class entropy. Experiments on real-world ADS-B and AIS datasets demonstrate that TA-MoE consistently outperforms prior methods in overall accuracy, macro-averaged F1 score, and tail-class recognition.

records.title: LPA-MoE: A Lightweight Period-Aware MoE Model for Time Series Forecasting in Data Centers
records.reason: Accurate time series forecasting is crucial for improving the operational efficiency and enabling energy savings for refrigeration units in data centers enabled by Internet-of-Things (IoT). However, time series data in real-world scenarios often contain multiple complex patterns, which challenge existing deep learning methods. While Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) architectures show promise for pattern decoupling in general forecasting tasks, their industrial applicability has not been fully investigated. This paper proposes LPA-MoE, a lightweight period-aware MoE model tailored for refrigeration in data center scenarios. LPA-MoE integrates three core components, including an FFT-based periodic embedding module to capture multi-scale periodic patterns, a gated lightweight TimesBlock for efficient local feature extraction and a sparse MoE routing mechanism to dynamically decouple heterogeneous temporal patterns. This design enables the model to achieve stronger representational capacity and lower computational overhead. Experimental results on realworld datasets from refrigeration units in IoT-enabled data centers validate that the proposed method not only significantly improves forecasting accuracy and stability on multi-pattern time series data but also exhibits excellent generalization capability.
